title: La ciudad
goal: Name places in town, say where you're going with ir a, and ask for and follow directions.

lessons.title: Around town
lessons.notes:
Many town words are close to English - **el restaurante, el hospital, la farmacia, el parque** - but watch the false friend **la biblioteca**: it's the library (a bookshop is la librería).
Compound names are built with **de**, main word first: **la estación de tren** (train station), **la parada de autobús** (bus stop).
To find something: **¿Dónde está la farmacia?** (a specific one) or **¿Hay una farmacia cerca?** (is there one nearby?). Hay + un / una for 'is there a...?', está for 'where is the...?'.
**El cajero automático** (or just **el cajero**) is the ATM.

sentences.en: Where is the pharmacy?
The hospital is far away.

sentences.es: Hay un parque cerca de mi casa.
sentences.en: There's a park near my house.
accept_en: There is a park near my home.
There's a park close to my house.

sentences.es: La biblioteca está en el centro.
sentences.en: The library is in the centre.
accept_en: The library is in the city centre.

sentences.en: Is there an ATM nearby?
accept_en: Is there a cash machine near here?
Is there an ATM close by?

sentences.es: La parada de autobús está allí.
sentences.en: The bus stop is over there.

sentences.es: El mercado está abierto los sábados.
sentences.en: The market is open on Saturdays.

sentences.es: La estación de tren está cerca del hotel.
sentences.en: The train station is near the hotel.
accept_en: The railway station is near the hotel.
The station is close to the hotel.

sentences.es: Mis hijos estudian en la escuela.
sentences.en: My children study at school.
accept_en: My kids study at the school.

sentences.en: The restaurant is closed today.

sentences.es: La iglesia es muy grande y bonita.
sentences.en: The church is very big and pretty.
accept_en: The church is very big and beautiful.
The church is very large and pretty.

lessons.title: Going places: ir a
lessons.notes:
**Ir** (to go) is irregular - learn it as it is:
**yo** voy · **tú** vas · **él / ella / usted** va · **nosotros** vamos · **ellos / ustedes** van
(Spain: vosotros **vais**.)
Where to? **a** (to): **Voy a la playa.** And **a + el** always squeezes into **al**: **Voy al parque** (never 'a el'). A la, a los, a las stay apart.
Ask **¿Adónde vas?** (where are you going to?). How you get there: **en** + transport (**en autobús, en tren, en carro**), but **a pie** (on foot). **¡Vamos!** on its own = let's go!

sentences.en: I'm going to the supermarket.
Where are you going?
We're going to the beach.

sentences.es: Ana va al trabajo en autobús.
sentences.en: Ana goes to work by bus.
accept_en: Ana takes the bus to work.

sentences.en: My parents are going to Mexico.
I walk to the park.
accept_en: I go to the park on foot.

sentences.en: Are you going by train or by car?
accept_en: Do you go by train or by car?

sentences.en: On Sundays we go to the market.
accept_en: We go to the market on Sundays.

sentences.en: I'm going to the pharmacy.
They're going to the cinema.

sentences.es: Después del trabajo voy al gimnasio.
sentences.en: After work I go to the gym.
accept_en: After work I'm going to the gym.

sentences.en: Do you want to go to the park?
accept_en: Would you like to go to the park?

lessons.title: Directions
lessons.notes:
Asking: **Perdón, ¿cómo llego a la estación?** (how do I get to the station?)
The answers you'll hear most:
**Sigue todo derecho** - keep going straight ahead (Spain: **todo recto**)
**Dobla a la derecha / a la izquierda** - turn right / left (Spain: **gira**)
**Está en la esquina** - it's on the corner
**dos cuadras** - two blocks (Spain: **manzanas**)
Sigue and dobla are friendly commands (tú) - you only need to understand them for now; unit 29 teaches commands. To a stranger people say **siga** and **doble**.
Place words: **al lado de** (next to), **enfrente de** (opposite), **detrás de** (behind), **entre** (between). De + el = **del**: al lado **del** banco.

sentences.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
accept_en: Sorry, how do I get to the station?

sentences.en: Keep going straight ahead for two blocks.
accept_en: Go straight on for two blocks.
Keep going straight for two blocks.

sentences.es: Dobla a la izquierda en la esquina.
sentences.en: Turn left at the corner.

sentences.es: El banco está a la derecha.
sentences.en: The bank is on the right.

sentences.es: La farmacia está al lado de la iglesia.
sentences.en: The pharmacy is next to the church.
accept_en: The chemist is next to the church.
The pharmacy is beside the church.

sentences.es: El parque está enfrente de la escuela.
sentences.en: The park is opposite the school.
accept_en: The park is across from the school.

sentences.es: El carro está detrás de la casa.
sentences.en: The car is behind the house.

sentences.es: La tienda está entre el banco y la farmacia.
sentences.en: The shop is between the bank and the pharmacy.
accept_en: The store is between the bank and the chemist.

sentences.en: It's on the corner.

sentences.es: Dobla a la derecha y sigue una cuadra.
sentences.en: Turn right and keep going for one block.
accept_en: Turn right and go one block.
Turn right and continue for a block.

lessons.title: Getting around
lessons.notes:
**Tomar** is the everyday verb for catching transport: **Tomo el metro. Tomamos un taxi.** (Spain says **coger**, but avoid that word in much of Latin America, where it's vulgar.)
A ticket is **el boleto** in most of Latin America and **el billete** in Spain. **De ida** is one-way, **de ida y vuelta** return.
Lost? **Estoy perdido / perdida** - it matches you, like cansado. **¿Está lejos?** (is it far?) - **No, está cerca, a cinco minutos** (five minutes away).
No 'a' for nationality-style words: **Somos turistas** (we're tourists).

sentences.en: Excuse me, I'm lost.
Is the airport far?

sentences.es: Un boleto de ida y vuelta, por favor.
sentences.en: A return ticket, please.
accept: Un billete de ida y vuelta, por favor.

sentences.en: I take the metro to work.
accept_en: I catch the subway to work.
I take the underground to work.

sentences.en: I'm going to the airport by taxi.
accept_en: I go to the airport by taxi.
I'm taking a taxi to the airport.

sentences.es: Voy en bicicleta a la escuela.
sentences.en: I go to school by bike.
accept_en: I ride my bike to school.

sentences.en: Where do I buy a ticket?
accept_en: Where can I buy a ticket?

sentences.es: No, está cerca, a cinco minutos.
sentences.en: No, it's close, five minutes away.
accept_en: No, it's near, five minutes away.

sentences.en: We're tourists from Australia.

sentences.es: Ana está perdida en el centro.
sentences.en: Ana is lost in the centre.
